# Takeout Photo: full site content (llms-full.txt)
> Plain-markdown version of https://takepho.com/ and its three guides, so LLM assistants can read the site without HTML. Source of truth: the HTML pages.

> Source: https://takepho.com/

# Turn your Google Takeout into a timeline of every trip you've taken.
Takeout Photo finds your holidays and day trips automatically, puts your photos on your Strava, Komoot or Garmin routes, and can move your library to Proton Photos. It runs on your Mac or Windows PC: your photos never go to our servers.

[Open the live demo](https://takepho.com/demo/#/timeline) [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe)

Demo: sample photos, nothing to install, no account.

Free to download · Lite is free for your 5 most recent holidays · Mac: Apple silicon, macOS 12+ · Windows 10/11 · [NAS (Docker)](https://takepho.com/self-host/) · [Windows portable zip](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64.zip).

Free to download. The Mac app is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. The Windows app isn't code-signed yet: on the first launch Windows shows "Windows protected your PC" — click "More info", then "Run anyway". The installed app updates itself automatically (checks daily, Settings → Updates; installs when the app quits); the portable zip doesn't — new versions are on the [releases page](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases).

- **Runs on your computer.** Your photos are never uploaded to our servers.
- **Free Lite plan.** No account, no licence.
- **Mac app signed and notarized by Apple.**
- **Pay once.** Lifetime licence, USD 25 / EUR 20.

The hero shows the Photos timeline app screenshot (the Rows timeline of the sample library, year cards with trip cards): [open it in the live demo](https://takepho.com/demo/#/timeline).

## Every trip you've taken, found for you (Photos timeline)
The Photos timeline reads your Takeout and works out where you lived, when you travelled and what you saw. Browse it as a timeline (rows, or one long scroll by year), on a map, trip by trip or as numbers.

- **All your trips on one map**: holidays, day trips and home periods are told apart automatically from your photo locations; each trip shows its places joined in the order you visited them, with towns and countries named from the GPS coordinates; add your Google Maps Timeline (Location History, with Lifetime or Yearly) and trips start and end when you really left and came home, photos without GPS get a location, and Travel shows your flights and long journeys
- **Each trip, day by day**: a day-by-day page per trip; on-device AI picks the best photos and a cover for each trip and stacks near-duplicates; your Strava, Komoot or Garmin activities appear on the day they happened; open any photo to see the full-resolution original, read straight from the archive
- **Your travels in numbers**: the Overview page counts your countries visited and holiday days per year, split by country, plus flights taken and kilometres flown once you add your Google Maps Timeline; holidays by country, and where you lived when

Make it yours (Lifetime and Yearly): rename and annotate trips, pick a cover, hide trips or photos; set or edit your homes and re-run trip detection (Lifetime and Yearly); add your partner's Takeout so their photos join the trips you shared (Yearly); photos flagged "Deleted in Google Photos" are listed so you can keep or remove them (Lifetime and Yearly); your edits (names, notes, homes, hidden photos) survive importing a newer export.

[More about browsing a Takeout as a timeline](https://takepho.com/google-photos-takeout/)

## Your photos on your Strava, Komoot and Garmin routes (Activities)
The Activities app matches the photos in your Takeout to your activities by capture time and puts each one on the GPS track.

- Every photo placed along the route with its distance and time ("km 12.3 · 10:42"); photos without GPS are placed by time
- Best photos, a photo strip and an elevation profile with a marker for every photo; splits and a link back to the activity on Strava
- Photos you already uploaded to Strava are shown too, with duplicates hidden
- All your routes are on one map, coloured by sport, with a heatmap mode; filter by sport, year, country, duration or "with photos"
- The Stats page totals distance, moving time and elevation per year and per sport, and counts how many activities have photos
- The link goes both ways: activities appear inside your trips, and each activity links to its trip
- Connecting your accounts: Strava through the official API with your own free Strava API app (a step-by-step guide is built in); Komoot and Garmin Connect with your own login; the same activity recorded on two services is shown once

[More about photos on your Strava activities](https://takepho.com/google-photos-strava/)

## Move your Google Photos to Proton Photos (Proton Photos sync)
The sync app uploads the Google Photos part of your Takeout to Proton Photos in full original quality, with the dates, places and albums intact.

- Keep the albums as they are in your Takeout, or get one album per detected trip
- Capture date, GPS, description, favourite and people are written from the sidecars into the files first, without re-encoding the pixels
- Files without a capture date are flagged, with one-click date suggestions
- Full original quality uploads through Proton's official Drive CLI
- Pause and resume at any time; an interrupted sync continues on the next start
- A sync never deletes anything in your Proton account; re-runs skip what is already in Proton; Revert sync moves what the app uploaded to the Proton trash
- Only your own photos: other people's Takeouts never go to Proton

[More about moving Google Photos to Proton Photos](https://takepho.com/google-photos-to-proton-photos/)

Every screen above is in the live demo, with sample photos: [Open the live demo](https://takepho.com/demo/#/timeline) [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe)

## Pricing
Start free: the demo and the sample library in the app need no account, and Lite is free for your 5 most recent holidays. Lifetime and Yearly unlock your whole library and all three apps; updates are free for everyone.

### Lite: free
- Your 5 most recent holidays in the photo timeline, plus the home periods and day trips in that span (the app shows "5 of N holidays").
- No account or licence needed.
- Import your own Takeout manually: a local folder of .tgz/.zip archives, including a newer export later.
- Read-only (no renaming, curating or hiding trips, no editing homes) and no automatic imports.
- Activity matching (Strava/Komoot/Garmin) and the Proton Photos move are on the paid plans.

[Download free](https://takepho.com/#download)

### Lifetime: USD 25 / EUR 20 one-time, no subscription
- All three apps: Photos timeline, Activities (Strava, Komoot, Garmin) and Proton Photos sync.
- Import your Takeout manually: from a folder on disk, a Google Drive link, or read-only Google sign-in.
- Unlocks your whole library, no photo limits: the rest of your photos are processed in the background, without re-importing.
- Importing a newer Takeout export rebuilds the library from it, and your edits (hidden photos, trip names and notes, homes, people) are kept.
- All app updates included.

[Download the app](https://takepho.com/#download) — Buy in the app: Settings → Account

then USD 12.50/year: renewals are 50% off, automatically

- Everything in Lifetime, and you keep Lifetime if you cancel.
- Automatic processing: the folder watcher imports new exports as they land, newer exports import incrementally (no rebuild), and you can add contributors (other people's Takeouts, e.g. a partner's).
- The first paid year includes the Lifetime licence: if you cancel, you keep it.

[Download the app](https://takepho.com/#download) — Buy in the app: Settings → Account

Not sure? Lifetime is enough unless you want newer exports imported automatically or a partner's photos in your trips.

Lite is free, no account needed. Prices for the paid plans include taxes. The currency is picked from your country at checkout: USD 25 (United States and rest of the world), EUR 20 (Europe), GBP 20 (United Kingdom), CHF 20 (Switzerland and Liechtenstein). Buy inside the app: open Settings → Account, sign in with Google or Apple, choose a plan and pay. Prices include taxes. Cancel any time from the app's "Manage subscription" button. For a refund, email hello@takepho.com and we will sort it out.

## From Takeout archive to timeline in three steps

### 1. Request your Takeout
[takeout.google.com](https://takeout.google.com) delivers your export as one or more archive files: takeout-001.zip, takeout-002.zip, ...

### 2. Takeout Photo processes it
On your computer, not in the cloud:

- Reads .zip/.tgz archives in place, without unpacking them
- Real dates, GPS and descriptions from the JSON sidecars
- Handles libraries of hundreds of GB; newer exports merge in
- Interrupted imports resume where they left off
- Your photos are never uploaded to our servers

### 3. Explore in Takeout Photo
- Photos timeline
- Activities
- Proton Photos sync

The built-in apps open for the data your export contains. The Takeout page shows what your export contains (products, archives, photos, videos and metadata files), and every import shows its steps as a checklist and picks up where it left off after a restart.


## Built for big libraries
Figures from the real library the app is developed against:

- **249 GB** of Takeout archives, about 34,000 photos
- **0 GB** unpacked: archives are read in place, originals are never copied
- **13 GB** of thumbnails, previews, index and database for that library
- **1 min** to re-read the inventory of 233 GB of archives (after the first import)

Browsing needs only the local previews; full-resolution originals are read from the archives on demand, so keep the archives reachable (in your folder or on Drive). When a newer export replaces an old one, remove the app's local copies of the old one with one button to free the space; files in your own folder and on Drive are never deleted. The AI model (about 578 MB) downloads once and runs on your computer, on the GPU when there is one.

## Runs where you keep your photos
The desktop app runs on your Mac or Windows. On a home server or NAS, run the Docker image with Docker Compose and open it in your browser on your network.

- **Mac**: Apple silicon Mac (M1 or later) with macOS 12 (Monterey) or later. Signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg)
- **Windows**: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The installer keeps the app up to date automatically; there is also a portable zip. [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe) (or the [portable zip](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64.zip)). See "Why does Windows show "Windows protected your PC" when I open the app?" in the FAQ for the first-launch warning.
- **NAS**: a Docker container on your home server or NAS, started with Docker Compose. Open it in the browser on your network. Same plans as the desktop app. [Self-hosting guide](https://takepho.com/self-host/)

## Private by design
- **Processed on your computer.** Your photos are never uploaded to our servers.
- **Read-only Google access.** Limited to the Takeout files you pick, and you can revoke it any time.
- **No tracking in the app.** No analytics and no ads.
- **Your accounts stay yours.** Activities and tracks from Strava, Komoot and Garmin are stored only on your computer.
[Read the full privacy policy](https://takepho.com/privacy.html)

## Coming next
- More sync destinations: Proton Photos is the first, others will follow
- Support for more of your Takeout: Google Drive and Google Docs files, not just the Google Photos part

## Frequently asked questions
**Is it a web app?** No. It is a desktop app for Mac and Windows, and there is a Docker image you can run on a NAS. Your photos stay on your computer unless you choose to sync them to Proton Photos.
**Is there a phone app?** No. Takeout Photo is a desktop app for Mac and Windows. If you run the Docker image on a NAS or home server, you can open it in the browser of any device on your network, including a phone.
**Which computers does it run on?** Mac: Apple silicon (arm64), macOS 12 (Monterey) or later; signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Windows: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
**How much disk space does it need?** The archives themselves, plus a small local library. For a real 249 GB Takeout with about 34,000 photos the app stores about 12.6 GB of thumbnails and previews, a 370 MB index and a 170 MB database. The archives are read in place and never unpacked or copied.
**Do I need to keep the Takeout archives after importing?** Yes, if you want full-resolution originals. Browsing uses local previews, but originals are read from the archives on demand, so keep them in your folder or on Drive.
**How does the app update?** Both apps update themselves. Mac: use "Check for Updates…" in the app menu, or let it check automatically (you can turn automatic checks off in Settings → Updates). Windows: the installed app checks for updates daily and installs them when the app quits (toggle in Settings → Updates, plus a "Check for updates now" button); while the exe isn't code-signed, updates are verified with an EdDSA signature. The portable zip doesn't update itself — download new versions from the [releases page](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases). Updates are free for everyone, no plan needed. [Release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases).
**Why does Windows show "Windows protected your PC" when I open the app?** The Windows app isn't code-signed yet, so on the first launch Windows shows that warning. Click "More info", then "Run anyway" — the app is safe to run. The installed app updates itself automatically (checks daily, Settings → Updates; installs when the app quits); the portable zip doesn't — new versions are on the [releases page](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases).
**Do I need to pay?** No, not for Lite: it is free for your 5 most recent holidays (photo timeline only, no account needed). A paid plan (Lifetime or Yearly) unlocks the full library with no photo limits and the other apps (activity matching, Proton Photos move).
**What is Lite?** Lite is the free plan: no account or licence needed. Import your own Google Takeout manually (a local folder of .tgz/.zip archives, including a newer export later) and get the photo timeline only, read-only, limited to your 5 most recent holidays plus the home periods and day trips in that span (the app shows "5 of N holidays"). Activity matching (Strava/Komoot/Garmin) and the Proton Photos move stay on the paid plans. Buying Lifetime or Yearly unlocks the whole library: the rest of the photos are processed in the background, without re-importing.
**Can I rename or hide trips?** Yes, with Lifetime or Yearly: rename a trip, add notes, pick its cover, hide trips or photos, and set your homes. Lite is read-only. Your edits are kept when you import a newer export.
**Do I need an account?** No, not for Lite (see "What is Lite?"). The app is also free to download and explore (the sample library in the app, or the [web demo](https://takepho.com/demo/)). A paid plan needs an account: sign in with Google or Apple from the app (Settings → Account). One account covers 2 devices (Mac or Windows).
**Does it work offline?** Yes. The app keeps a signed entitlement on your computer and refreshes it about weekly, so it needs internet at least once a month.
**What happens if an import is interrupted?** Interrupted work resumes automatically: if the app is closed, the computer restarts or the app updates mid-import or mid-processing, it picks up where it left off on the next start. Already imported items are skipped, an import that stopped has a "Resume import" button, and every import shows its steps as a checklist with the current step live.
**Does it need my Google password?** No. Sign-in happens on Google's own page, and you can revoke access any time at [myaccount.google.com/permissions](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions).
**What about the Google Photos API?** Google no longer lets apps read a whole Photos library, so Google Takeout is the way to get all your photos with their metadata. Takeout exports include everything you need.
**Does it show videos and HEIC photos?** HEIC photos are decoded on your computer and shown like any other photo. The timeline shows photos today; videos in your Takeout are counted in the inventory and uploaded by the Proton Photos sync.
**Why are the dates wrong after unzipping a Google Takeout?** The file's own timestamp is often the export date; the real capture date and GPS live in the .json sidecar next to each photo. Takeout Photo reads those sidecars, so dates and places are right. See [browsing a Takeout as a timeline](https://takepho.com/google-photos-takeout/).
**Can I see my Google Photos on my Strava, Komoot or Garmin activities?** Yes. The Activities app matches your Google Photos from the Takeout to each activity by capture time and places every photo along the GPS track ("km 12.3 · 10:42"). It works with Strava, Komoot and Garmin Connect. See [photos on your Strava activities](https://takepho.com/google-photos-strava/) — Komoot and Garmin Connect work the same way.
**How do I move my Google Photos to Proton Photos?** The sync app moves the Google Photos part of your Takeout into Proton Photos in full original quality, keeping albums (or making trip albums) and writing dates, GPS and descriptions from the JSON sidecars into the files first. See [moving Google Photos to Proton Photos](https://takepho.com/google-photos-to-proton-photos/).
**Does it work with Google Drive or Docs from my Takeout?** Not yet. Today it uses the Google Photos part of your Takeout, plus Location History where your export has it. Support for Google Drive and Google Docs files is coming, and the sync app will add more destinations beyond Proton Photos.
**Can I add someone else's Takeout, like my partner's?** Yes. With the yearly plan you can add contributors (other people's Takeouts, e.g. a partner's), so their photos attach to the trips you shared.
**What happens when the yearly plan ends?** You keep the Lifetime licence (the first paid year includes it). Manual imports keep working forever, and importing a newer export still rebuilds your library with your edits kept. The automatic-processing features (folder watcher, incremental imports of newer exports, new contributors) stop while the subscription is inactive; existing contributors stay visible. You can re-subscribe any time.
**Does the yearly price go up?** No — it goes down. The first year is billed at the full price (e.g. USD 25), and every renewal after that is automatically 50% off (USD 12.50 per year; EUR 20 → EUR 10, GBP 20 → GBP 10, CHF 20 → CHF 10). Nothing for you to do; it renews at half price until you cancel.
**How do I cancel or get a refund?** Cancel any time from the app's "Manage subscription" button; the plan runs to the end of the paid year. For a refund, email hello@takepho.com and we will sort it out.

# Google Photos Takeout viewer: browse your export as a timeline
A Google Photos Takeout is the set of .zip or .tgz archives you download from takeout.google.com: year folders and album folders full of photos and videos, plus a small .json file next to each photo that holds the real capture date, GPS location and description. Takeout Photo is a desktop app for Mac and Windows that reads those archives in place (without unzipping) and turns them into a private timeline of trips, places and maps on your own computer.
Desktop app for Mac and Windows  [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Try the demo](https://takepho.com/demo/#/timeline). Free to download and explore. Lite is free: import your own Takeout manually and browse your 5 most recent holidays; a plan (USD 25 one-time, or yearly at USD 25 the first year then USD 12.50/year) unlocks the whole library ([pricing](https://takepho.com/#pricing))

## What is inside a Google Photos Takeout?
When you export Google Photos with [Google Takeout](https://takeout.google.com), Google splits the export into one or more archive files (`.zip` or `.tgz`) chosen by the file size you pick (for example 50 GB per file). Inside the archives you get a `Takeout/Google Photos/` folder with one folder per year, your album folders, and your photos and videos.
Next to almost every photo there is also a small JSON sidecar file with the same name plus `.json`. That sidecar is where Google stores the metadata that matters: the real capture time (`photoTakenTime`), the GPS coordinates (`geoData`), the description you wrote, people in the photo, and more. Takeout Photo builds an inventory of what is in your export (which products, which archives, what sizes) so you can see what you have before you open anything.

## Why do dates look wrong when you just unzip a Takeout?
If you unzip a Takeout and sort the photos by file date, many of them look wrong, often showing the day you made the export, not the day the photo was taken. The file's own timestamp is unreliable; the truth is in the `.json` sidecar next to the photo. If a tool ignores the sidecars, every date, place and description is lost or wrong.
Takeout Photo reads the JSON sidecars, so dates and locations are right: each photo shows when it was taken and where, and towns and countries are named from the GPS coordinates by reverse geocoding.

## How Takeout Photo reads your Takeout in place
You never have to unpack the archives. Download the [app](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) (Mac: Apple silicon, macOS 12 or later; Windows: 10 or 11, 64-bit) and point it at a local folder, a Google Drive link, or sign in with Google and pick the archive files in Google's picker; access is read-only and limited to the files you choose. The app reads the `.zip` and `.tgz` files directly, so libraries of hundreds of GB work without filling your disk twice. It's free to download and explore the sample library; with Lite (free) you can import your own Takeout from a local folder and see your 5 most recent holidays, and a paid plan unlocks the whole library. See [pricing on the home page](https://takepho.com/#pricing).
If you schedule regular Takeout exports, new archives are picked up and merged automatically with the yearly plan (incrementally, without duplicating photos you already have). With the Lifetime plan you re-import a newer export manually, and your edits (hidden photos, trip names and notes, homes, people) are kept. With Lite (free) you can also import a newer export manually later — it stays limited to your 5 most recent holidays.

## Trips, places and maps
The Photos app detects where you live and when you moved, plus day trips and holidays, so you can browse your life by trip instead of by raw date. Browse it as a timeline (rows, or one long scroll by year), on a map, trip by trip, or as numbers: the Overview page counts your countries and charts your holiday days per year; with your Google Maps Timeline it also counts flights and kilometres flown.

**Improve trip detection with your Google Maps Timeline (Location History).** Photos only show where you were when you pressed the shutter; your Timeline knows where you went in between. Add it and trips are detected from your actual movements, so each one starts and ends when you really left and came home. Photos without GPS get a location from it, and real routes are drawn on the map using open street data. With your Google Maps Timeline imported, switch on Travel to see flights and long journeys on the map. The file stays on your computer.

Google now keeps Timeline on your phone instead of in new Takeouts, so export it once: on Android, Settings → Location → Location services → Timeline → Export Timeline data; on iPhone, Google Maps → your profile picture → Settings → Personal content → Export Timeline data. Copy the .json file to your computer and import it under Location history in the Photos app's Settings.
AI curation runs on your own machine: it groups near-duplicates and picks the best shots for each trip. You can also add other people's Takeouts (for example your partner's) so their photos attach to the trips you shared.

## How to export Google Photos with Google Takeout

1. Go to [takeout.google.com](https://takeout.google.com) and sign in with your Google account. 
2. Deselect everything, then select only **Google Photos**. 
3. Click "Next step", choose the delivery method (a download link by email, or directly to your Google Drive), the file type (`.zip` or `.tgz`) and the maximum file size. 
4. Click "Create export" and wait for Google's email; large libraries can take hours or days. 
5. Download the archives, or copy the Drive link, and point the app at them.    
## Private by design
Everything is processed locally on your computer; your photos are never uploaded to our servers. Google access is read-only and only ever touches the files you pick. See the [privacy policy](https://takepho.com/privacy.html).

## Frequently asked questions
**What exactly is a Google Photos Takeout?** It is the archive Google gives you at takeout.google.com: one or more .zip or .tgz files containing your Google Photos (photos, videos, album folders, year folders) plus a JSON sidecar file next to each photo with its real capture date, GPS location and description.
**Do I have to unzip the Takeout archives first?** No. Takeout Photo reads .zip and .tgz archives in place, from a local folder, a Google Drive link, or by signing in with Google and picking the files. You can keep the export exactly as Google delivered it.
**Why are the photo dates wrong after unzipping a Takeout?** Because the file's own timestamp is often the export date, not the capture date. The real capture time and GPS coordinates live in the .json sidecar next to each photo, and Takeout Photo reads those, so dates and places come out right.
**Can it handle a very large photo library?** Yes: archives are read in place without unpacking, so libraries of hundreds of GB are handled without needing the same space again on disk.
**What happens when a new scheduled Takeout export arrives?** With the yearly plan, new archives are picked up and merged automatically (incrementally, without duplicating photos). With the Lifetime plan you re-import a newer export manually: the library is rebuilt from it and your edits (hidden photos, trip names and notes, homes, people) are kept. With Lite (free) you can also import a newer export manually later — it stays limited to your 5 most recent holidays.
**Is anything uploaded to a server?** No. Everything is processed locally on your computer and your photos are never uploaded to our servers. Google sign-in, if you use it, is read-only and limited to the files you pick.

# See your Google Photos on your Strava activities
Your photos live in Google Photos and your routes live in Strava, and nothing connects the two. Takeout Photo's Activities app links them on your own computer: it reads your Google Photos from a Takeout export, syncs your activities from Strava (official API, OAuth), Komoot or Garmin Connect (your own login), and matches each photo to an activity by capture time, placing it along the GPS track.
Desktop app for Mac and Windows  [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Try the demo](https://takepho.com/demo/#/activities/1). Free to download and explore. The photo timeline is free with Lite (your 5 most recent holidays); matching photos to your Strava, Komoot or Garmin activities needs a plan (USD 25 one-time, or yearly at USD 25 the first year then USD 12.50/year, [pricing](https://takepho.com/#pricing))

## Why photos and routes end up in two places
You take photos with your phone, so they end up in Google Photos. You record your runs, rides and hikes with Strava, Komoot or Garmin Connect, so the routes end up there. Your activity app shows the photos *you uploaded to it* (Strava shows the ones you uploaded to Strava), but the rest of your camera roll (the photos from your Google Photos library) stays invisible on the activity. Takeout Photo closes that gap locally, without uploading anything anywhere.

## How the matching works
The Activities app connects to your account: with Strava it uses the official Strava API and OAuth — you create your own free Strava API application (the app includes a step-by-step guide) and authorize Takeout Photo; with Komoot or Garmin Connect you sign in with your own login (Komoot login; Garmin Connect email and password, plus an MFA code if you have one enabled) over their unofficial APIs. The app then syncs your activities from every connected provider; activities that appear in more than one service are de-duplicated. For each activity, your Google Photos from the Takeout are matched by capture time: every photo taken during the activity is placed at the point along the GPS track where it was taken, shown as "km 12.3 · 10:42".
Because the capture time comes from the Takeout JSON sidecars (not the file timestamp), the match is based on when the photo was really taken.

## Komoot and Garmin Connect work the same way
The Activities app is not Strava-only. Sign in with your Komoot login, or with your Garmin Connect email and password (plus an MFA code if you have multi-factor authentication enabled), and your Komoot or Garmin Connect activities sync exactly like Strava ones: matched to your Takeout photos by capture time and placed along the GPS track (GPS photos by distance to the track, photos without GPS interpolated between their neighbours), shown together with your Strava activities on one map of all your routes, in one activities list, with stats and a heatmap, and de-duplicated when the same activity appears in more than one service. Komoot and Garmin Connect use unofficial APIs; Takeout Photo is not affiliated with or endorsed by Komoot or Garmin.

## What you get
All your routes are on one map, coloured by sport, with a heatmap mode, and the Stats page totals distance, time and elevation per year.

- **A map of all your routes**, coloured by sport, with a heatmap mode. 
- **Filters** by sport, year, country, and "with photos". 
- **Activity pages** with the route, the best photos for that activity, and a photo strip. 
- **Stats per year**, and start/end place names for each activity. 
- **Photos you already uploaded to Strava** are shown too; duplicates of your Takeout photos are hidden so nothing appears twice. 
- **A link back to the activity** on its provider (Strava, Komoot or Garmin Connect), plus an optional embed where the provider offers one. 
- Activities are linked to the **trips in the Photos app**, so a weekend ride and the holiday around it connect.    
## How to connect your activity accounts

1. Export your Google Photos with [Google Takeout](https://takeout.google.com) (see [how to export and browse a Takeout](https://takepho.com/google-photos-takeout/)). 
2. [Download the app](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) (Mac: Apple silicon, macOS 12 or later; Windows: 10 or 11, 64-bit) and point it at the archives; free to explore the sample library. Lite (free) imports your own Takeout for the photo timeline; activity matching needs a plan ([pricing](https://takepho.com/#pricing)). 
3. Connect a provider in the Activities app: **Strava** — create your own free Strava API application (a step-by-step guide is built into the app) and authorize Takeout Photo to read your activities via OAuth; **Komoot** — sign in with your Komoot login; **Garmin Connect** — sign in with your Garmin email and password, and enter the MFA code if you have multi-factor authentication enabled. 
4. Start the sync.    
## Privacy
Everything is processed locally on your computer; your photos are never uploaded to our servers. For Strava the app reads activities and GPS tracks over the official API, read-only, and does not modify your Strava account. For Komoot and Garmin Connect the app talks directly from your computer to Komoot / Garmin with your own login (unofficial APIs); your credentials and tokens are sent only to Komoot / Garmin and stored only on your device — we never receive them. See the [privacy policy](https://takepho.com/privacy.html).

## Frequently asked questions
**Do I need to create my own Strava API application?** Yes, for Strava. Strava requires every app to use its own free API application; the Takeout Photo app includes a step-by-step guide for creating one and authorizing it via OAuth. Komoot and Garmin Connect do not need this: you just sign in with your own login.
**Does it work with Komoot or Garmin Connect too?** Yes. The Activities app also syncs your Komoot activities (sign in with your Komoot login) and your Garmin Connect activities (email and password, plus an MFA code if you have multi-factor authentication enabled), over their unofficial APIs. Matching works the same way, and activities from all providers are shown together and de-duplicated.
**How are my photos matched to an activity?** By capture time. Each Google Photo taken while the activity was recorded — on Strava, Komoot or Garmin Connect — is placed along the activity's GPS track at the point matching its time (for example "km 12.3 · 10:42").
**Does it upload my photos to Strava, Komoot or Garmin Connect?** No. The app works locally and never uploads your photos to any of them: for Strava it shows the photos you already uploaded to Strava as well, and hides duplicates of the same photos from your Takeout so nothing appears twice.
**Which activities can have photos?** Any activity with a GPS track and a time range. The map colours routes by sport and you can filter by sport, year, country, or only activities with photos.
**Is my activity data kept private?** Yes. Strava activities are read over the official Strava API with read-only access; Komoot and Garmin Connect are contacted directly from your computer with your own login (unofficial APIs), and their credentials and tokens stay on your device. Everything is processed on your own computer, and your photos are never uploaded to our servers or to the activity providers by the app.

## Also works with your Takeout

- [Google Photos Takeout viewer](https://takepho.com/google-photos-takeout/): browse the export itself as a timeline of trips and places. 
- [Move your Google Photos to Proton Photos](https://takepho.com/google-photos-to-proton-photos/): keep albums and metadata when you leave Google. 
- [Takeout Photo home](https://takepho.com/): the photo timeline app.   [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Try the demo](https://takepho.com/demo/#/activities/1)

# Move your Google Photos to Proton Photos: with albums and metadata
Uploading a plain Google Takeout to Proton Photos loses the album structure and often the dates and locations, because that metadata lives in the JSON sidecars next to each photo, not in the files themselves. Takeout Photo's sync app moves the Google Photos part of your Takeout into Proton Photos (Proton Drive) in full original quality (writing the capture date, GPS location, description, favourites and people from the sidecars losslessly into the files first) using Proton's official open-source Drive CLI.
Desktop app for Mac and Windows  [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Try the demo](https://takepho.com/demo/#/sync/albums). Free to download and explore. The photo timeline is free with Lite (your 5 most recent holidays); moving your photos to Proton Photos needs a plan (USD 25 one-time, or yearly at USD 25 the first year then USD 12.50/year, [pricing](https://takepho.com/#pricing))

## Why a plain Takeout upload loses dates, places and albums
In a Google Photos Takeout, the photo files themselves often carry the export date as their timestamp, and the real capture date, GPS coordinates, description, favourites and people are stored in the `.json` sidecar next to each photo. If you upload the archive as-is, Proton Photos sees the wrong dates and places, and the Google album structure does not become Proton albums. Takeout Photo reads the sidecars and fixes the files before uploading, so Proton shows the correct dates and places.

## Two ways to organise the import

- **"As in the Takeout"**: your Google Photos albums become Proton albums, and everything not in an album goes to the Photos timeline. 
- **"Trip albums"**: one Proton album per detected trip, containing that trip's photos and videos, named "{Type} {place} – {Month YYYY}" — for example "Holiday Alcúdia, Spain – May 2025". A trip you renamed keeps its custom name, and albums created by an earlier sync are renamed on the next sync.  Before anything is uploaded, the app writes the capture date, GPS location, description, favourite flag and people from the Takeout JSON sidecars into the files, losslessly. Everything is uploaded in full original quality.

## How the upload works
Uploads go through Proton's official open-source [Proton Drive CLI](https://github.com/ProtonDriveApps/sdk/tree/main/cli), which runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. The app installs it for you with checksum verification, and you sign in to Proton in your browser. Pause and resume at any time; an interrupted sync continues on the next start. Re-runs are safe: files that are already in Proton are skipped, and a sync never deletes anything in your Proton account. If you change your mind, Revert sync moves what the app uploaded to the Proton trash.
If a sync is interrupted — the app is closed, or the computer or server restarts mid-sync or mid-revert — it resumes automatically on the next start. The sync card lists the failures of the current sync ("Failures in this sync"), with the failures of earlier syncs one click away.

## Windows alternative: the import folder
On Windows you can instead use an import folder for the Proton Drive Windows app: Photos → Import → "Import a folder". Note that with this route a photo that belongs to several albums lands in only one album. The Proton Drive Mac app has no Photos import, so on macOS the sync uses the CLI.

## Step by step

1. Export Google Photos with [Google Takeout](https://takeout.google.com) (see [how to export a Takeout](https://takepho.com/google-photos-takeout/)). 
2. [Download the app](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) (Mac: Apple silicon, macOS 12 or later; Windows: 10 or 11, 64-bit) and point it at the archives: with Lite (free) a local folder, with a paid plan also a Drive link or sign in with Google and pick the files (read-only). Free to explore the sample library; the Proton Photos move needs a plan ([pricing](https://takepho.com/#pricing)). 
3. In the sync app, choose the layout: "as in the Takeout" or "trip albums". 
4. Let the app install the Proton Drive CLI (checksum-verified) and sign in to Proton in your browser. 
5. Run the sync. You can re-run it any time; what is already in Proton is skipped, and a sync never deletes anything in your Proton account.
## What is never synced
Other people's Takeouts (for example your partner's) are never synced to your Proton account. Everything is processed locally on your computer first; the only destination of the upload is your own Proton Photos. Your photos are never uploaded to our servers. See the [privacy policy](https://takepho.com/privacy.html).

## Frequently asked questions
**Does it upload in original quality?** Yes: the Google Photos part of your Takeout is moved to Proton Photos in full original quality, not a compressed copy.
**Do my Google Photos albums survive the move?** Yes. With the "as in the Takeout" layout, Google Photos albums become Proton albums and the rest goes to the Photos timeline. Alternatively, the "trip albums" layout creates one album per detected trip, named "{Type} {place} – {Month YYYY}" — for example "Holiday Alcúdia, Spain – May 2025".
**What happens to dates, GPS and descriptions?** Before upload, the capture date, GPS location, description, favourite flag and people from the Takeout JSON sidecars are written losslessly into the files, so Proton Photos shows the correct dates and places.
**Is it safe to run the sync again?** Yes. Re-runs skip what is already in Proton, and a sync never deletes anything in your Proton account. If you change your mind, Revert sync moves what the app uploaded to the Proton trash.
**Do I need the Proton Drive desktop app?** Not necessarily: the app uploads with Proton's official open-source Proton Drive CLI on Linux, macOS and Windows. On Windows there is also the import-folder route via the Proton Drive app; the Proton Drive Mac app has no Photos import, so macOS uses the CLI.
**Are other people's Takeouts synced to my Proton account?** No. Other people's Takeouts are never synced to your Proton account. Only your own Google Photos part of your Takeout is moved.

## Also works with your Takeout

- [Google Photos Takeout viewer](https://takepho.com/google-photos-takeout/): browse the export itself as a timeline of trips and places. 
- [See your Google Photos on your Strava activities](https://takepho.com/google-photos-strava/): photos matched to each activity along the GPS track. 
- [Takeout Photo home](https://takepho.com/): the photo timeline app.   [Download for Mac](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-macos-arm64.dmg) [Download for Windows](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/releases/latest/download/TakeoutPhoto-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Try the demo](https://takepho.com/demo/#/sync/albums)

# Run Takeout Photo on a NAS with Docker Compose
The Docker image is public at `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho` and runs on x86 (amd64) and 64-bit ARM (arm64) servers. It gives you the same app, and the same three apps (Photos timeline, Activities, Proton Photos sync), running on your NAS or home server, open in a browser on your network. Your scheduled Takeout exports can land in a folder on the NAS.

## What you get
The same app as the desktop version, served from your NAS and opened in a browser at `http://<nas-address>:8080`. Everything is processed on the NAS; your photos are never uploaded to our servers.

## Plans and account
The same [plans and prices as the desktop app](https://takepho.com/#pricing): Lite is free for your 5 most recent holidays (photo timeline only, no account needed), and Lifetime/Yearly unlock the whole library and all the apps. For a paid plan, sign in from Settings → Account in the browser and choose a plan; the NAS counts as one of your account's 2 devices and needs internet at least once a month to refresh the licence.

## Requirements
- Docker Engine with Compose v2.24 or later (Synology Container Manager, Unraid, TrueNAS, or any Linux box).
- An x86-64 (amd64) or 64-bit ARM (arm64) CPU, for example an ARM Synology or a Raspberry Pi 4/5 with a 64-bit OS. The NVIDIA GPU image is x86-64 only.
- 4 GB RAM free for the container; 8 GB recommended for big libraries.
- Disk for the data folder (thumbnails and indexes, plus about 600 MB for the AI model on first use).
- Optional: an NVIDIA GPU (driver 580 or later, NVIDIA Container Toolkit) with the image `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho-cuda:latest`.

## Quick start
Save this as `docker-compose.yml` on the NAS:

```yaml
services:
  app:
    image: ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${TIMELINE_PORT:-8080}:8000"
    volumes:
      - ${TIMELINE_DATA:-timeline-data}:/data
      - ${TIMELINE_MODELS:-timeline-models}:/app/models/clip
      - ${TAKEOUT_DIR:-./takeout}:/takeout:ro
volumes:
  timeline-data: {}
  timeline-models: {}
```

Then `docker compose up -d` and open `http://<nas-address>:8080` in your browser. The example uses `:latest`, which always points at the newest release; every release also has a pinned tag, e.g. `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho:1.2.0` and `ghcr.io/ecyshor/takepho-cuda:1.2.0`.

## Folders
- `/data`: the library database, thumbnails and indexes. Back this up.
- `/app/models/clip`: the downloaded AI model. It can be re-downloaded, no backup needed.
- `/takeout`: your Takeout archives, mounted read-only. On Synology, point `TAKEOUT_DIR` at for example `/volume1/takeout`.

## Security
Security: the published compose file turns on Google sign-in (AUTH_ENABLED=true; restrict accounts with AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS). Even so, keep it on your home network or behind a VPN, and never forward the port to the internet.

## Updating and backups
Update with `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. Stopping or updating the container mid-import is safe (e.g. `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`) — the import and processing pick up where they left off when the container starts again. For backups, copy the data volume (`timeline-data`).

## Synology, Unraid, TrueNAS
In Synology Container Manager, Unraid or TrueNAS, create a Compose project (or stack) from the file above and start it.

## Help
If something does not work, [open a support issue](https://github.com/ecyshor/takepho.com/issues/new) with where the app runs, the version, what happened and the steps to reproduce.
